chapter: Europe 1933, New York Cotton Club, Hodges group
title: Recording with Gleason, off-Broadway shows and joining CBS
summary: After Ellington he recorded with Jackie Gleason, played Nancy Walker and Carol Channing shows, and joined the CBS staff after Hodges retired.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: wasn't along there was it? No. No. That was -- I don't know where Sears got that record. I mean where he recorded that record. I don't remember. We did so much you see. I don't remember. Not only recorded with Ellington -- I recorded with so many other groups and things that I get all -- you know I can't remember.
You know, as I told you at first, I don't have any records or listings of where the records or when they were made.
Who have you recorded with besides -- I mean after your time with (inaudible) Ellington.
Oh, gee. I did some with Gleason.
Jackie Gleason and his big outfit. And then several -- or we'd just go on record dates -- many record dates. And then I did a couple of off-Broadway shows.
One with Nancy Walker down at the Phoenix Theater.
I don't know -- I don't remember. Then another with -- who was the big-eyed girl? "Diamonds Are A Girl's Best Friend."
Carol Channing. On Broadway at the Wintergarden. Did a show with her. And things like that.
You just -- oh, and then I went into CBS staff for four years. About four years and a half.
Was that -- after Johnny retiring wasn't it?
